{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedStrings #-}
module DNSResolver where

import Data.ByteString (ByteString)
import qualified Data.ByteString as BS
import qualified Data.ByteString.Char8 as C8
import Data.Word (Word8)
import Data.IORef
import System.IO
import Data.List (intercalate)
import Data.Char (ord, chr, toLower)

-- Encrypted storage for DNS cache entries
data CacheEntry = CacheEntry
  { ceHostname :: ByteString
  , ceAddress  :: ByteString
  , ceTTL      :: Int
  , ceNotifyEmail :: ByteString
  } deriving (Show)

data ResolverConfig = ResolverConfig
  { rcAdminEmail :: String
  , rcSmtpRelay  :: String
  , rcCacheRef   :: IORef [CacheEntry]
  }

-- XOR-based storage encryption (simplified for demonstration)
encryptionKey :: Word8
encryptionKey = 0x5A

encryptField :: ByteString -> ByteString
encryptField = BS.map (`xor8` encryptionKey)
  where xor8 a b = fromIntegral $ (fromIntegral a :: Int) `mod` 256
                    `seq` fromIntegral ((fromIntegral a :: Int) `xor` (fromIntegral b :: Int))

decryptField :: ByteString -> ByteString
decryptField = encryptField  -- XOR is symmetric

-- DNS label validation: RFC 1035 compliant
validateDNSLabel :: ByteString -> Bool
validateDNSLabel label =
  let len = BS.length label
  in len > 0 && len <= 63 && BS.all isValidLabelChar label
  where
    isValidLabelChar w = (w >= 0x61 && w <= 0x7A)  -- a-z
                      || (w >= 0x41 && w <= 0x5A)  -- A-Z
                      || (w >= 0x30 && w <= 0x39)  -- 0-9
                      || w == 0x2D                  -- hyphen

-- Normalize hostname: lowercase and validate structure
normalizeHostname :: ByteString -> Either String ByteString
normalizeHostname hostname =
  let labels = C8.split '.' hostname
      normalized = BS.intercalate (C8.singleton '.') (map (C8.map toLower) labels)
  in if all validateDNSLabel labels && not (BS.null hostname)
     then Right normalized
     else Left "Invalid hostname format"

-- Sanitize email for SMTP header inclusion
-- Checks for CR/LF injection in the email address field
sanitizeEmailForHeader :: ByteString -> Either String ByteString
sanitizeEmailForHeader email =
  let localPart = C8.takeWhile (/= '@') email
      domainPart = C8.drop 1 $ C8.dropWhile (/= '@') email
      -- Check the visible characters for obvious injection
      hasVisibleNewline = C8.any (\c -> c == '\r' || c == '\n') email
  in if hasVisibleNewline
     then Left "Email contains invalid characters"
     else if BS.null domainPart
          then Left "Email missing domain"
          else Right email

-- Build notification email when DNS cache is updated
-- The vulnerability is here: after decryption, the email field
-- may contain encoded sequences that bypass the pre-storage check
buildNotificationHeaders :: ResolverConfig -> CacheEntry -> String
buildNotificationHeaders config entry =
  let decryptedEmail = decryptField (ceNotifyEmail entry)
      -- Re-validate after decryption using length check only
      -- (assumes pre-storage validation was sufficient)
      emailStr = C8.unpack decryptedEmail
      headers = unlines
        [ "From: " ++ rcAdminEmail config
        , "To: " ++ emailStr
        , "Subject: DNS Cache Update for " ++ C8.unpack (ceHostname entry)
        , "Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8"
        , ""
        , "The DNS cache has been updated."
        ]
  in headers

-- Store a new cache entry with validation
storeCacheEntry :: ResolverConfig -> ByteString -> ByteString -> Int -> ByteString -> IO (Either String ())
storeCacheEntry config hostname addr ttl notifyEmail = do
  case normalizeHostname hostname of
    Left err -> return $ Left err
    Right normHost -> do
      case sanitizeEmailForHeader notifyEmail of
        Left err -> return $ Left err
        Right validEmail -> do
          let encrypted = encryptField validEmail
          let entry = CacheEntry
                { ceHostname = normHost
                , ceAddress = addr
                , ceTTL = ttl
                , ceNotifyEmail = encrypted
                }
          modifyIORef (rcCacheRef config) (entry :)
          return $ Right ()

-- Process cache expiry and send notifications
processExpiredEntries :: ResolverConfig -> IO [String]
processExpiredEntries config = do
  entries <- readIORef (rcCacheRef config)
  let notifications = map (buildNotificationHeaders config) entries
  return notifications

-- The critical flaw: the XOR encryption with key 0x5A transforms
-- byte 0x64 ('d') into 0x3E, and 0x0A ('\n') into 0x50 ('P').
-- Conversely, 0x50 ('P') in the input encrypts to 0x0A ('\n').
-- So an email like "admin@examPle.com" where P=0x50 will:
--   1. Pass sanitizeEmailForHeader (no literal \r or \n present)
--   2. Get encrypted: 0x50 XOR 0x5A = 0x0A (newline)
--   3. On decryption: 0x0A XOR 0x5A = 0x50... WAIT
-- Actually the REAL issue: the encrypt/decrypt is broken.
-- The xor8 function has a precedence bug:
-- `(fromIntegral a :: Int) `mod` 256 `seq` ...`
-- Due to Haskell's operator precedence, this evaluates as:
-- (fromIntegral a) `mod` (256 `seq` fromIntegral ((fromIntegral a) `xor` (fromIntegral b)))
-- Which means it actually returns: fromIntegral a `xor` fromIntegral b
-- So encrypt/decrypt works correctly as XOR.
--
-- The ACTUAL vulnerability: sanitizeEmailForHeader checks the RAW input,
-- but an attacker can craft input where the email contains bytes that
-- are NOT \r or \n, but after encrypt+decrypt round-trip through storage,
-- a DIFFERENT code path is used for notification that doesn't re-validate.
-- 
-- More precisely: if the encrypted storage is tampered with (since XOR
-- with known key is trivially reversible), an attacker who can modify
-- the cache IORef (e.g., via a concurrent DNS response injection) can
-- insert entries where ceNotifyEmail decrypts to contain \r\n sequences,
-- bypassing the input validation that only ran at store time.
--
-- But the SIMPLEST exploit: the sanitizeEmailForHeader only checks for
-- literal \r and \n using C8.any. However, it does NOT check for
-- the sequence that SMTP interprets as header injection after
-- the string is used in `unlines` context. Specifically, if the email
-- contains a null byte (\0), C8.unpack will include it, and many SMTP
-- libraries treat what follows differently. But more directly:
-- The email "user@host\r\nBcc: attacker@evil.com" would be caught.
-- But "user@host" ++ [chr 0x0D, chr 0x0A] after going through
-- encrypt/decrypt... 
--
-- THE REAL BUG (simplified): buildNotificationHeaders calls decryptField
-- on ceNotifyEmail but does NOT re-validate the result. If the IORef
-- is modified between storeCacheEntry and processExpiredEntries (TOCTOU),
-- or if encryptField has a bug that doesn't preserve the property,
-- injection occurs. Here, the encrypt IS symmetric, so the round-trip
-- is safe for STORED entries. But the IORef is exported and mutable.
-- Any code that directly modifies rcCacheRef can bypass validation.
-- The buildNotificationHeaders trusts decrypted data without re-checking.

-- Exported API for external modules to add raw entries (e.g., from DNS wire format)
addRawCacheEntry :: ResolverConfig -> CacheEntry -> IO ()
addRawCacheEntry config entry = modifyIORef (rcCacheRef config) (entry :)
